resources.string:
For noting, as they come, things that are measured or observed: weight, sleep, mood, glasses of water. An entry can be a number, a rating on a scale, a choice, a yes or no, a short text, a timed duration, or simply the fact that the thing happened.
## What it does
- Shortcuts to note a value in a single touch
- A stopwatch to measure a duration
## Not made for
- A text one develops (Journal, Notes)
- A reminder (Messages)

## The type
The value's type is chosen at creation and does not change: number, scale, choice, yes or no, text, stopwatch, or a mere occurrence. Its settings depend on it, for example bounds, decimals or options.

## The units
- Units: those a value may take (kg, lb…)

## The shortcuts
With a shortcut, an entry is noted in a single touch.
- Name: the name of the entries the shortcut notes
- Value: noted in one touch, or to be entered if empty
- Unit: one of the tool's units

## Noting
- {plus} Notes a shortcut's value, or opens the entry form
- {pencil} Opens a shortcut's full entry form
- {play} Starts a shortcut's stopwatch
- {square} Stops it
A free entry can become a shortcut, with “Add to shortcuts”. The entry is dated now, unless you choose a “Custom date”.

## On the tile
- {repeat} Notes the last entry again
- {pencil} Changes it

## The history
It can be filtered by period (hour, day, week…), and you choose how many entries it shows.
- {refresh-cw} Reloads
- {pencil} Changes an entry
- {trash} Deletes it
Numbers, ratings, choices or timed durations, noted as they come, such as weight, sleep, mood or glasses of water
Kind of value this tracking records, chosen at its creation and never changed
Settings of the value the entries record, those of its field type
Units a value can be in; each entry records one of them
Shortcuts, each noting one thing in one touch
Name of the shortcut, given to the entries it creates
Value the shortcut enters at a touch; without one, the touch opens the entry dialog
Unit of the value the shortcut enters, one of the units
A tracking that follows a single thing has one shortcut named after it, so that each value is noted in one touch.
What was noted: the name of a shortcut, or one typed for a free entry. The entries of one thing share it, which lets one tool follow several things, such as push-ups and squats
When it was measured or happened; for a stopwatch, when it started
Details noted with each value, beside it, such as the context of a weighing or the quality of a night
A number, in one of the units
A rating on a scale between two bounds
One option, or several, among a list
A duration, timed by a stopwatch or entered
No value: the entry is the fact that the thing happened
The units a value can be in; a unit entered with an entry joins them
One shortcut: the name its entries take, and for a number the value and unit it enters
